newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bills end lower, pull mid-bond yields down.
newsitem.headline: NZ bills end lower, pull mid-bond yields down.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close

* Higher NZ dollar pushes 90-day rates lower at close
* Short, mid bonds rally slightly, long end meets selling
* Politics, US developments seen key to flow-driven market
New Zealand rates continued to head lower at Tuesday's close as the currency recovered from last week's plunge of almost one US cent.
Ninety-day bill rates lost some of the impetus they enjoyed in early trade, but still ended 10 basis points lower and dragged yields in short and mid bonds down around three points.
The short end was also boosted by a two-year, NZ$100 million eurokiwi issued overnight by the Council of Europe.

The Kiwi was at around 0.7068/75 in late afternoon trade, after dropping below US70 cents from around US71 cents late last week after the Reserve Bank of New Zealand said conditions were tighter than necessary.
Long bonds encountered selling interest on the day and ended a couple of points weaker, but dealers said flows were small.
"I think the market is obviously still in bull mode -- it's just a matter of whether we can crack some pretty crucial levels here," a Wellington dealer said.
"We're struggling with that seven percent level in the mid curve, and with 7.25 percent in the long end," he added.

Dealers expected the market to be flow-driven over the next couple of days, with little domestic economic news on the horizon. The fate of the short end was seen largely pinned to movements in the New Zealand dollar, with the possibility of profit-taking after the Kiwi's bounce back up.
Political coalition negotiations start in earnest this week in the quest to form a new government, but dealers did not expect the talks to turn up fresh news for some time.
The U.S. is seen holding considerable sway over local developments, with a raft of influential economic data and the general election next month.
